title: claude tile data
description: Data for the bundled `claude` tile: one niri desktop. The tile is DATA-DRIVEN — waybar always references `claude`, and the template renders by what you send: an `items` array of rows (1 → single layout, 2 → stacked dual layout with a shared shortcut gutter), each row being either a Claude session or an ordinary window — so a MIXED desktop (one session + one plain app) is expressible. The older feeds still validate and render: a bare `sessions` array, or the flat `app`/`app_icon`/`title` fields for one window. Feed it as the module's `exec` stdout (JSON) or static `text`. Each property notes REAL (from the claude-status-db daemon) vs MOCK (synthesize it).

anyOf.comment: Unified rows: one or two windows on this desktop, session or app, in any mix.
Claude layout (legacy): one or two sessions on this desktop.
Window layout (legacy): the leftmost window's icon + label.

shortcut.description: MOCK. The niri desktop's shortcut number, shown first (big, in a shared left gutter when two rows).

active.description: Whether this is the focused/active niri desktop → the accent 'card'.

is_claude.description: LEGACY, accepted and ignored. It used to select the layout: true (or omitted) → a Claude desktop (uses `sessions`); false → an ordinary window (uses `app`/`app_icon`). Rows are now self-describing, so old payloads still carrying it render fine — but it decides nothing, and new feeds should omit it.

items.description: The window(s) on this desktop, as unified rows (1 → single layout, 2 → stacked dual layout). A row is either a Claude SESSION row (`state` required) or an APP row (`app` + `app_icon` required); mix them freely. Supersedes `sessions` and the flat `app`/`app_icon`/`title` fields — send the desktop's windows and the tile adapts, you never pick the layout.

anyOf.comment: Session row — `state` required; `kind` may say so explicitly.
App row — `app` + `app_icon` required; `kind` may say so explicitly.

kind.description: Optional row discriminator. Omit it and the tile infers: a row with `state` is a session, a row with `app` is an app.

state.description: REAL (sessions.state). Session rows only, and required there. Drives this row's indicator: working=Claude mascot deep-orange, prompt=blinking '?' (and the WHOLE tile pulses if ANY row is prompt), idle=fade bar (see idle_level) + idle_ago, shell=mascot electric-cyan, empty=no indicator, just the bare shortcut (the producer's placeholder for a desktop with no session and no window — never an idle bar).

idle_ago.description: REAL-derived. When state=idle: time since active (e.g. '12m'), beside the bar. Keep it short.

folder.description: REAL (basename of sessions.cwd). Session rows only.

app.description: App rows only, and required there: the app/window label, after its inline icon.

app_icon.description: App rows only, and required there: a bundled icon name (e.g. 'code') or an absolute path to an .svg, drawn inline before the label.

title.description: MOCK. The window title. Wrapped (one row) or tickered (two rows).

unpushed.description: MOCK. Session rows only. Unpushed commit count; shown as ↑N after the folder (hidden when 0 or idle).

fleet.description: REAL. Present when this row stands for a set of BACKGROUND AGENTS rather than one conversation — either the desktop is running the `claude agents` view (scope=whole, every agent on the machine) or its session spawned them (scope=owned). NOTE the row stays a SESSION row: `state` is still required and still drives the indicator and the tile-wide pulse, so a template that ignores `fleet` renders it as an ordinary session. That is deliberate — `kind` is a closed enum, so there is no `kind: "fleet"`. The row's `state` is derived from the fleet: prompt when any agent awaits a human, working, shell when the fleet is blocked on itself, else idle aged on the FLEET's newest activity.

awaiting.description: Agents waiting on a HUMAN. Non-zero is what makes the row `prompt` and pulses the tile.

blocked.description: Blocked on another agent, NOT on a person.

demands.description: One entry PER AGENT, worst first — this is the bead strip, in order. The template paints one bead per entry, coloured by demand, and groups them where the demand changes.

neediest.description: Name of the agent that set the worst demand. Can be long: an agent spawned without --name is titled from its intent (a real one reads `Review baroque database replica configuration`), so the template clips.

needs.description: That agent's ask, VERBATIM and unclipped — a real value ran ~600 characters (a whole AskUserQuestion with its options). The producer deliberately does not truncate; clipping is the template's job, and it must clip or a wrapped ask grows the tile past its fixed height.

scope.description: `whole` = a console desktop (the agent view is machine-wide); `owned` = this desktop's session spawned them; `herd` = a herdr workspace, i.e. one multiplexer pane group.

sessions.description: LEGACY (still supported): the Claude session(s) on this desktop (1 → single layout, 2 → stacked dual layout). Equivalent to an `items` array of session rows. Send the desktop's sessions; the tile adapts — you never pick the layout, the data does.

state.description: REAL (sessions.state). Drives this session's indicator: working=Claude mascot deep-orange, prompt=blinking '?' (and the WHOLE tile pulses if ANY session is prompt), idle=fade bar (see idle_level) + idle_ago, shell=mascot electric-cyan, empty=no indicator, just the bare shortcut.

idle_ago.description: REAL-derived. When state=idle: time since active (e.g. '12m'), beside the bar. Keep it short.

title.description: MOCK. The session window title. Wrapped (single-session) or tickered (dual).

unpushed.description: MOCK. Unpushed commit count; shown as ↑N after the folder (hidden when 0 or idle).

title.description: LEGACY flat window feed (used only when neither `items` nor `sessions` is present): the window title (shown wrapped under the app). Rows carry their title inside items[].title instead.

app.description: LEGACY flat window feed (used only when neither `items` nor `sessions` is present): the app/window label.

app_icon.description: LEGACY flat window feed (used only when neither `items` nor `sessions` is present): a bundled icon name (e.g. 'code') or an absolute path to an .svg.
